title: Hashcat — OffSec mode quick reference
inline_answer:
| Hash | `-m` |
|---|---|
| MD5 | `0` |
| SHA1 | `100` |
| NTLM (pwdump / SAM / secretsdump) | `1000` |
| NetNTLMv1 | `5500` |
| Net-NTLMv2 (Responder) | `5600` |
| md5crypt `$1$` | `500` |
| sha512crypt `$6$` (/etc/shadow) | `1800` |
| bcrypt `$2*$` | `3200` |
| Kerberoast TGS-REP `$krb5tgs$` | `13100` |
| AS-REP `$krb5asrep$` | `18200` |
| KeePass `.kdbx` | `13400` |

```
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

title: Crack NTLM — hashcat -m 1000
inline_answer:
**NTLM = `-m 1000`** (SAM / secretsdump / pwdump format `user:rid:LM:NT:::` — feed only the NT field).

```
hashcat -m 1000 nt.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

Not Net-NTLMv2 (`-m 5600`) — that is the Responder/network hash, a different thing.

title: Crack Net-NTLMv2 (Responder) — hashcat -m 5600
inline_answer:
**Net-NTLMv2 = `-m 5600`** (the hash Responder/`ntlmrelayx` capture gives you).

```
hashcat -m 5600 netntlmv2.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

If it will not crack, **relay it instead** — see the Net-NTLMv2 capture & relay section.

title: Crack /etc/shadow — sha512crypt -m 1800
inline_answer:
Linux shadow hashes by prefix: `$6$` sha512crypt = **`-m 1800`**, `$1$` md5crypt = **`-m 500`**, `$5$` sha256crypt = **`-m 7400`**, `$y$`/`$2*$` yescrypt/bcrypt = **`-m 3200`**.

```
hashcat -m 1800 shadow_hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

For John: `unshadow /etc/passwd /etc/shadow > unshadowed.txt` first.

title: Crack KeePass .kdbx — hashcat -m 13400
inline_answer:
**KeePass = `-m 13400`**.

```
keepass2john Database.kdbx > kp.hash      # remove the "Database:" prefix from the line
hashcat -m 13400 kp.hash /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

Then open the DB with the cracked password (`kpcli --kdb=Database.kdbx`) and loot every entry.

title: John the Ripper — basic syntax + *2john
inline_answer:
```
john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --format=<fmt> hash.txt
john --show --format=<fmt> hash.txt
```

Extractors (file → crackable hash): `ssh2john id_rsa`, `zip2john f.zip`, `keepass2john f.kdbx`, `office2john f.docx`, `pdf2john f.pdf`. `--format` must match how you cracked it for `--show`.

title: Hydra — HTTP POST login form
inline_answer:
Capture the login POST in Burp, note the body params and a string only present on **failure**:

```
hydra -L users.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt <IP> http-post-form \
  "/login.php:username=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=Invalid"
```

`F=` = failure string, `S=` = success string (use one). `https-post-form` for 443. Single user spray: `-l admin`.

title: Cracked a password — now spray it everywhere
inline_answer:
**Every cracked/found credential is sprayed against every target and every protocol immediately** — this loop is where most OffSec points come from.

```
crackr.sh   <hashfile>          # crack
sprayr.sh   --from-creds        # spray the new cred across SMB/WinRM/SSH/RDP/MSSQL/LDAP
```

Do not sit on a credential. Reuse is the intended path far more often than a fresh exploit.

title: Identify a hash fast
inline_answer:
Prefix tells you most of it: `$1$`=md5crypt, `$5$`=sha256crypt, `$6$`=sha512crypt, `$2y$/$2b$`=bcrypt, `$krb5tgs$`=Kerberoast, `$krb5asrep$`=AS-REP, `aad3b435...:hash`=NTLM (use the second half), `$DCC2$`=domain cached.

```
hashid -m '<hash>'        # suggests the hashcat -m
name-that-hash -t '<hash>'
```
